title: Psychosocial and social-needs problems (ICD-10-CM Z codes)
summary: Social and life circumstances that affect mental health, written as plan problems with the matching ICD-10-CM Z codes (Z55 to Z65 and nearby) for reference. Z codes describe circumstances, not the person, and are never a diagnosis.

problems.label: Unstable or unsafe housing
definitions: Is behind on rent or mortgage payments, has received an eviction notice, or expects to lose current housing in the coming months.
Is staying with others for now, in a shelter, a vehicle or another place not meant for living, or lives in housing without safe heat, water or power.
longTermGoals: The client has safer, more stable housing, or a clear plan and support to get there, and the rest of the plan fits their housing situation.

shortTermObjectives.text: In the first 2 sessions, name the most urgent housing need with the client (for example a court date, a place to stay tonight or unsafe repairs) and agree on 1 concrete step for the coming week.

By week 2, with consent, connect the client to at least 1 housing resource (for example 211, a local housing agency, or legal aid for eviction questions) and confirm at the next session whether contact happened.
Fit the rest of the plan to the housing situation (for example session times, where between-session practice can happen and how handouts are kept), and review the fit at each plan review.

zCodes.label: Housing instability, housed, with risk of homelessness
Housing instability, housed, homelessness in past 12 months

problems.label: Not enough money for food, utilities or other basics
definitions: Runs out of food, or money for food, before the end of the month, or skips meals because of cost.
Struggles to pay for utilities, medicines, transport or other basics, or has had a utility shut-off notice.
longTermGoals: The client's basic needs are better met through benefits and community resources, and money stress is part of the shared picture rather than a source of blame.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 2, ask about food and money needs in a matter-of-fact way and, with consent, connect the client to at least 1 resource (for example food assistance, help with utility bills or 211) within 2 weeks.
By week 4, with the client's agreement, arrange a benefits check (for example nutrition assistance, health coverage or utility programs) through a case manager, social worker or community agency.
Over weeks 3 to 8, use structured problem solving on 1 money-related stressor every 2 weeks and note what changed.

zCodes.label: Financial insecurity, difficulty paying for utilities

problems.label: Job loss, insecure work or strain at work
definitions: Has lost a job or fears losing it, or works hours or conditions that leave little time for rest, family or treatment.
Describes conflict, harassment or unfair treatment at work that affects mood, sleep or safety.
longTermGoals: The client has a plan for work or income that fits their health and values, and work stress is easing or better managed.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 3, map the work situation with the client (what is in their control, what is not, and what support exists) and choose 1 area to work on first. For long-term work stress or a planned return to work, add the work stress and return-to-work module.

By week 4, with consent, link the client to at least 1 employment or income resource that fits (for example a job center, vocational rehabilitation, or the Job Accommodation Network for questions about workplace adjustments).

If unfair treatment or harassment at work is described, by week 4 share information about the client's options (for example the employer's complaint process or the US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission) and leave the decision to the client.

zCodes.label: Other physical and mental strain related to work

linkOuts.publisher: Job Accommodation Network (US Department of Labor)

problems.label: Living alone or cut off from people, with loneliness
definitions: Has few or no people to talk with or rely on in a usual week, and describes feeling lonely or left out.
Has lost social roles or contact, for example after a move, retirement, illness or a death.
longTermGoals: The client has more regular, meaningful contact with people or communities of their choosing.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 3, map current and past connections (people, groups, faith or community places, online communities) and choose 1 to strengthen.
Over weeks 3 to 10, take at least 1 planned social step a week (for example a call, a group, volunteering or a class), starting with the easiest step and building up.
By week 6, notice at least 2 thoughts that hold back contact (for example that others would not want to hear from the client) and test each with a small experiment.

problems.label: Stress from discrimination, exclusion or adjusting to a new culture
definitions: Describes being treated unfairly, excluded, harassed or threatened because of race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, age or another part of who they are.
Is adjusting to a new country or culture and describes stress from language, the loss of familiar supports, changed roles or uncertainty about legal status.
longTermGoals: The client feels heard and supported, has ways of responding to discrimination-related stress that fit their values and community, and has the practical and legal information they want.

shortTermObjectives.text: In the first 3 sessions, invite the client to describe experiences of discrimination or adjustment in their own words, and note how these affect them without questioning whether they happened.
By week 6, name at least 2 sources of strength or belonging (for example family, community groups, faith, cultural practices or affirming organizations) and plan 1 contact with one of them.
If the client wants it, by week 4 share information about reporting or legal options (for example a civil rights office, an immigration legal service or legal aid) and leave the choice to the client.

zCodes.label: Target of (perceived) adverse discrimination and persecution

problems.label: Strain from caring for a relative or friend who needs care at home
definitions: Gives regular care to a family member or friend with illness, disability or memory problems, and has little time for rest, health or work.
Describes exhaustion, guilt, resentment or worry about the person they care for.
longTermGoals: The client has more support and breaks, looks after their own health, and feels more able to manage the caring role.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 3, list the caring tasks and who helps with each, and choose 1 task to share or hand over.
By week 4, with consent, connect the client to at least 1 caregiver resource (for example respite care, a caregiver support line or a support group).
Over weeks 3 to 10, schedule at least 1 short break or self-care activity a week and rate stress (0-10) before and after.

zCodes.label: Dependent relative needing care at home

problems.label: Legal problems, or returning to the community after incarceration
definitions: Faces court dates, probation or parole conditions, immigration proceedings, custody disputes or other legal processes that add stress and take time.
Has recently been released from jail or prison and is working on housing, work, health care and reconnecting with family.
longTermGoals: The client knows where to get legal help, can meet legal obligations, and has support through the transition.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 2, list upcoming legal dates and obligations with the client and plan how therapy fits around them (for example session times and transport).
By week 3, with consent, connect the client to legal aid or their attorney for legal questions, and keep the clinician's treating role separate from any legal or evaluation role.
For a client returning from incarceration, by week 2 check that medicines, health coverage and a primary care appointment are in place, and link to local reentry services.

zCodes.label: Problems related to other legal circumstances
Problems related to release from prison

problems.label: Abuse or control by a partner or former partner
definitions: Describes a partner or former partner who hurts, threatens, controls, monitors or isolates them, or who controls money or access to care.
Changes plans, appointments or contact with others out of fear of how a partner will react.
longTermGoals: The client is safer, knows their options and has support, and makes their own decisions about the relationship at their own pace.

shortTermObjectives.text: In private, without the partner present, the clinician asks about safety in the relationship. If abuse is described, the clinician and client make a relationship safety plan, separate from any suicide safety plan; the clinician makes every judgment about danger, and nothing here rates it.
By the next session, share hotline information in a way that is safe for the client (for example memorized, or saved under another name) and confirm the client knows how to reach emergency help.

Throughout treatment, keep the plan and any written materials safe from a partner's view (for example nothing sent home that names the abuse), and offer no couples sessions while abuse or coercive control is present; review both at each plan review.

zCodes.label: Encounter for mental health services for victim of spousal or partner abuse
Personal history of adult intimate partner abuse

collaborativeNote: Write these problems with the client and in their words. Z codes describe circumstances, not the person, and are recorded only when the client's situation fits and recording helps their care; the code titles are official ICD-10-CM wording and never question the client's experience. Confirm each code in the current ICD-10-CM code set before use. Do not add names or other identifying details. Resource only. Not a substitute for clinical judgment.
